# Building an abap2UI5 app

**Read `references/building-apps.md` next to this file (the framework's
guide, shipped with this skill) — it is the complete
self-contained guide** (template, lifecycle, builder verbs, binding rules,
events, popups, navigation, portability rules, validation tooling). This
skill is the trigger and the checklist; the guide is the content.

**Before writing one from scratch, ask whether it exists.** `abap2UI5/samples`
holds 150 working apps, each linted, rendered and downported to three
releases — a value help, a tree, navigation between two apps, a dynamic table
typed at runtime. Reading one beats reproducing it, and beats any snippet: the
sample is gated, a snippet is a copy somebody has to keep in step.

- With the [MCP server](https://github.com/abap2UI5/mcp-server): the `examples`
  tool queries that catalogue (`examples { query: "value help f4" }`) and
  hands back the class to read. Its neighbour `capabilities` answers the other
  question — whether a UI5 *control* can be expressed at all — out of
  samples-controls' 622 ports.
- Without it: [SAMPLES.md](https://github.com/abap2UI5/samples/blob/main/SAMPLES.md)
  is the same catalogue as a page.

The rules that go wrong most often. Each is one line here and a section of
the guide — read the section before you rely on the line.

- **One class implements `z2ui5_if_app`; `main( client )` runs once per
  roundtrip and is ONE `IF`/`ELSEIF` chain**, so exactly one arm runs:
  `IF client->check_on_init( ).` seeds and displays, `ELSEIF
  client->check_on_navigated( ).` displays, `ELSEIF client->check_on_event( ).`
  dispatches. The navigated arm is not optional — it is the roundtrip a
  called app or a value help hands control back on. An app with nothing to
  seed drops the init arm. Never separate `IF` blocks, never one nested in
  another (guide §2; the linter's `missing-view-display-on-navigated`,
  `redundant-init-display`, `separate-lifecycle-ifs`).
- **Ask the lifecycle with the call itself**: `IF client->check_on_init( ).`,
  never `IS INITIAL` / `IS NOT INITIAL`. A negative branch, and every other
  `abap_bool`, is compared: `= abap_false`.
- **PUBLIC attributes are serialized, browser-visible state.** Bound data
  only; everything else PROTECTED.
- **Build views with `z2ui5_cl_ui5_view_builder`** (`ele`/`tag`/`a`/`end`/
  `stringify`). The legacy `z2ui5_cl_xml_view` is frozen — never in new code.
- **`a( )` has three value parameters**: `v` for constants, bindings and
  events; `b` for a boolean from an ABAP variable (`abap_true` in `v`
  serializes as `X`); `t` for text that carries data, which the builder
  escapes so a `{` in it is not read as a binding (guide §3).
- **The chain's layout is strict and machine-checked — the `view-chain-layout`
  skill is the single source of the rules**, the `factory( )` shape that goes
  with each chain shape included (the linter's `chain-house-layout` rule:
  `npm run check:abap2ui5` reports,
  `npm run fmt:chains` applies). Write the chain, run the formatter, read the
  diff.
- **Bind with `client->_bind( var )`**, display-only included; `_bind_edit`
  is obsolete. Row-template fields bind as `` `{UPPERCASE}` ``. Never write a
  model path as a text literal. A value the view shows is bound, not baked
  into the view — changed bound data is pushed automatically, and
  `view_model_update( )` does nothing (guide §4).
- **Events**: `client->_event( `NAME` )`, dispatched with
  `CASE client->get_event( ).`. Client-resolved arguments are `$`-prefixed;
  an argument that carries data goes on a wire with
  `s_ctrl-check_arg_literal = abap_true`; a per-keystroke wire (`liveChange`,
  `liveSearch`, `sliderChange`) sets `s_ctrl-check_queue_last` (guide §5).
- **Popups**: `popup_display( val = … )`, but `popover_display( xml = …
  by_id = … )`. A button that only closes is
  `follow_up_action( val = cs_event-popup_close )`, not a backend event
  (guide §6).
- **Thin frontend**: business logic is computed in ABAP and bound, never put
  into a formatter. UI5 1.71 is the floor — check "available since"
  (the `ui5-check` skill).
- **The app checks its own authorizations** at the top of `main`.
- Validate with the abap2UI5-linter
  (`npx --yes @abap2ui5/linter <file>`); iterate without a SAP
  system via the mcp-server (`deploy_app` → `build_backend` → `run_app`,
  then `interact_app` to drive the event branch and `run_unit_tests` for
  the class's own test double — guide §9 has the tooling and the double).
- Before you finish, go through sections 1 and 2 of the `abap-check` skill —
  the abapGit round trip and activation. They catch what a green lint does
  not; its other sections are for the cases their headings name.
- The API contract is `src/02/z2ui5_if_client.intf.abap` in
  [abap2UI5/abap2UI5](https://github.com/abap2UI5/abap2UI5/blob/main/src/02/z2ui5_if_client.intf.abap) — when unsure about
  a method or a `cs_event` action, read it there; the `follow_up_action`
  abapdoc documents the full frontend-action catalog. For a signature alone,
  the generated index is enough: `references/client-api.md` next to this
  file,
  every signature in one short file, the obsolete ones apart.
